plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, bright flower head made up of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. The heads track the sun when young. Widely grown as an ornamental and as a crop for seeds and oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide in temperate regions including the US, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually made of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers arranged in a spiral pattern following the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower that produces dense, arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It forms large colonies in meadows, roadsides, and open fields, and is an important late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects. The real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial whose crocus-like flowers appear in autumn without any leaves. The foliage emerges the following spring and dies back by early summer. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and damp grasslands of Europe, from the UK to central Europe; grown in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: It is nicknamed 'naked ladies' because the flowers bloom without leaves. It is the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden ball-shaped flower clusters. It blooms at the end of the southern winter and into spring, brightening the Australian bush.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated every September 1, the first day of spring.
